name: Tramadol
subclass: Opioid agonist with serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibition
description: Tramadol (Ultram) facts: uses, dosing basics, seizure and serotonin syndrome risks, interactions, overdose, withdrawal, and how to get it legally.
quick: Tramadol is a prescription pain medicine that acts as a weak opioid and also raises serotonin and norepinephrine levels. It is a Schedule IV controlled substance. It is often thought of as mild, but it can cause addiction, seizures, serotonin syndrome, and fatal overdose.
facts: Pain severe enough to require an opioid
Tablets, extended-release tablets and capsules, oral solution
CYP2D6 (to the more potent O-desmethyltramadol) and CYP3A4

blocks.p: Tramadol is approved for adults with pain severe enough to require an opioid when other treatments are inadequate. Extended-release forms are for long-lasting pain needing daily treatment.[[1]]

It relieves pain in two ways: its metabolite O-desmethyltramadol activates opioid receptors, and tramadol itself blocks reuptake of serotonin and norepinephrine, like some antidepressants. This dual action explains its distinctive risks.

The figures below come from the FDA-approved label and describe how prescribers typically use tramadol. They are not personal dosing advice. A prescriber sets the dose for each person and adjusts it over time.[[1]]

rows: Start 25 mg a day, increase by 25 to 50 mg every 3 days to 50 to 100 mg every 4 to 6 hours

sections.q: What are the risks and side effects of tramadol?

boxed.title: FDA boxed warnings
items: Tramadol exposes users to risks of addiction, misuse, and abuse, which can lead to overdose and death.
Life-threatening slowed breathing can occur, especially when starting treatment or after a dose increase.
Accidental ingestion, especially by children, can cause a fatal overdose.
Use with benzodiazepines or other central nervous system depressants, including alcohol, can cause profound sedation, slowed breathing, coma, and death.
Prolonged use during pregnancy can cause neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome, which may be life-threatening if not recognized and treated.
Ultra-rapid CYP2D6 metabolizers can have life-threatening breathing problems; tramadol is contraindicated in children under 12.[[2]]
Drugs that affect CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 can change tramadol levels and cause overdose or seizures.

blocks.p: **Common side effects** include dizziness, nausea, constipation, headache, drowsiness, and sweating.[[1]]

**Seizures** can occur even at recommended doses, and the risk rises at high doses, with antidepressants, and in people with epilepsy or head injury. **Serotonin syndrome**, low blood sugar, and low sodium are other recognized risks.[[1]]

sections.q: What does tramadol overdose look like?

blocks.p: Tramadol overdose can cause sleepiness, slow breathing, pinpoint pupils, seizures, and a dangerously fast heartbeat. Seizures may happen even after naloxone restores breathing.[[1]][[3]]

emergency.title: If someone may have overdosed
items: Call 911 if the person is unresponsive, cannot be woken, has blue or gray lips, or is breathing slowly or not at all.
Give naloxone (Narcan or a generic nasal spray, sold without a prescription) into one nostril. If there is no response after 2 to 3 minutes, give another dose.
If you are trained, give rescue breaths. Otherwise place the person on their side so they do not choke.
Stay with them. Naloxone can wear off before tramadol does, so the overdose can return even after the person wakes up.
Most states have Good Samaritan laws that protect people who call 911 for an overdose from some drug charges.

sections.q: What is tramadol withdrawal like, and how long does it last?

blocks.p: People who take tramadol regularly for more than a few weeks become physically dependent, even when they take it exactly as prescribed. Dependence is not the same as addiction, but it means stopping suddenly causes withdrawal.[[1]]

timeline.title: Early symptoms
timeline.text: Anxiety, restlessness, yawning, sweating, runny nose, watery eyes, and muscle aches.

timeline.title: Peak withdrawal
timeline.text: Diarrhea, stomach cramps, nausea and vomiting, goosebumps, dilated pupils, fast heartbeat, and strong cravings. Rarely dangerous in healthy adults, but dehydration can be serious.

timeline.title: Lingering symptoms
timeline.text: Poor sleep, low mood, low energy, and cravings can continue for weeks. Tolerance falls quickly, which raises the risk of overdose if use restarts.

blocks.warn: After a break, the body loses tolerance within days. Returning to a previous dose of tramadol can cause a fatal overdose.

blocks.p: The FDA warns against stopping opioids abruptly in people who are physically dependent. A prescriber can taper the dose gradually, often by 10% or less per month for long-term users, and medicines such as clonidine or lofexidine can ease symptoms. For opioid use disorder, buprenorphine and methadone cut the risk of death roughly in half.[[4]]
Because tramadol also acts like an antidepressant, some people get unusual withdrawal symptoms such as anxiety, panic, confusion, tingling, or hallucinations in addition to typical opioid withdrawal.

sections.q: How do you get tramadol legally in the US?

blocks.p: In the United States, tramadol is a Schedule IV controlled substance. The only legal way to get it is with a prescription from a clinician registered with the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), filled by a licensed pharmacy. Depending on state law, that can be a physician, nurse practitioner, or physician assistant.[[5]]

ul: **Refills:** a Schedule IV prescription can be refilled up to five times within six months of the date it was written. After that, a new prescription is needed.[[6]]

**Telehealth:** federal flexibilities let DEA-registered clinicians prescribe Schedule II to V medicines after a telemedicine visit, without a prior in-person exam, through December 31, 2026. A permanent DEA rule was under final review in late 2026. State rules can be stricter.[[7]]
**Monitoring:** prescribers and pharmacists in most states check a prescription drug monitoring program, a database of controlled-substance prescriptions, before prescribing or dispensing.

**Pharmacies:** a legitimate pharmacy always requires a valid prescription, has a licensed pharmacist available, and is licensed in the state it ships to. The FDA's BeSafeRx tool and the NABP's safe pharmacy list help confirm a pharmacy is real.[[8]][[9]]
**Cost:** generic tramadol is inexpensive and widely covered.

blocks.p: **Traveling:** keep the medicine in its original pharmacy container and carry a copy of the prescription. Check the rules of the destination country before travel, because many countries restrict controlled medicines or require a permit.

Yes, but only with a valid prescription and only from a pharmacy licensed in your state. Many licensed pharmacies, including mail-order pharmacies run by insurers, fill tramadol prescriptions online and ship them. Buying tramadol from a website that does not require a prescription is illegal, and the product is often fake.[[8]][[10]]

steps: A clinician evaluates you in person or by telemedicine and decides whether tramadol is appropriate.
The prescription goes to a pharmacy
Prescriptions for controlled medicines are usually sent electronically, straight from the prescriber to the pharmacy you choose.
The pharmacy checks and fills it
A pharmacist verifies the prescription and your identity, then dispenses the medicine in person or by mail.

blocks.p: **Signs that an online seller is illegal:**

ul: It sells tramadol with no prescription, or after only a short online questionnaire.
It takes orders through social media, messaging apps, or email.
It asks for payment in cryptocurrency, gift cards, or money transfers.
It has no US street address, no state pharmacy license, and no pharmacist to speak to.
Its prices are far below those of ordinary pharmacies, or it ships from another country.

blocks.p: The FDA's BeSafeRx tool links to each state's license lookup, and the National Association of Boards of Pharmacy lists verified online pharmacies.[[8]][[9]]

faq: Yes. Its main metabolite activates opioid receptors, which is why it is a controlled substance and can cause addiction and overdose.
Yes, even at normal doses. The risk is higher above 400 mg a day, with antidepressants, and in people with a seizure disorder.
Can you take tramadol with antidepressants?
Only with care. Combining it with SSRIs, SNRIs, or tricyclics raises the risk of serotonin syndrome and seizures; it must not be taken with MAOIs.
How long does tramadol stay in your system?
Its half-life is 6 to 7 hours. Urine tests typically detect it for 1 to 4 days.
Is tramadol weaker than other opioids?
It is less potent per milligram, but it has caused many overdose deaths, and its seizure and serotonin risks do not apply to most other opioids.
